topic: Template Specialization and Type Deduction in Function Calls
explanation: In modern C++, template specialization allows developers to define custom behaviors for specific template parameter types, enabling optimized or specialized implementations. When combined with type deduction (via auto, decltype, or template argument deduction), C++ can automatically infer the correct template instantiation based on the function call or variable assignment. This mechanism enhances code flexibility and type safety, especially in generic programming, by allowing the compiler to select the most appropriate template version for a given type, including user-defined types or specialized cases.
